1	`BVList.v` is a Coq library for dependently typed bitvectors. It consists of a raw 
2	bit-vector type representing simply-typed bit-vectors, and a dependently-typed
3	bit-vector type that is generated by instantiating a functor (also defined in the 
4	library) with the raw bit-vector module.
5	
6	`InvCond.v` consists of the proofs of the 19 equivalences over raw bitvectors.
7	
8	`DepInvCond.v` consists of the same proofs over dependently-typed bit-vectors. 
9	
10	Many of the proofs in `BVList.v` and `InvCond.v` benefit from the
11	recostruction tactics of the [Coqhammer](https://github.com/lukaszcz/coqhammer) tool.
12	However, one does not need to install Coqhammer to be able to compile the library,
13	since all such tactics are in `Reconstr.v`.
14	
15	Compilation requires Coq version 8.20.0. To compile, run in `root`:
16	1. `coq_makefile -f _CoqProject -o Makefile`
17	2. `make`
18	
19	For more detailed installation instructions including Coq installation instructions, 
20	see [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md).
21

# Installation
Installation of packages necessary to check proofs of invertibility conditions in Coq.

## Requirements
- The library is designed to work on computers equipped with a POSIX (Unix or a clone) operating system. It is known to work under GNU/Linux (i386 and amd64) and Mac OS X.

- [Coq 8.20.0](https://github.com/coq/coq/tree/v8.20)

- [Coqhammer](https://github.com/lukaszcz/coqhammer)

## Installation of Packages using opam

### Install opam

We recommended to install the required packages from
[opam](https://opam.ocaml.org). Once you have installed opam on your system you
should issue the following command:

```bash
opam init
```

which will initialize the opam installation and prompt for modifying the shell
init file.

Once opam is installed you should still issue

```bash
eval `opam config env`
```

(this is not necessary if you start another session in your shell).

You need to have OCaml version >= 4.11.1 and Coq version 8.20.0.

> **Warning**: The version of Coq that you plan to use must have been compiled
> with the same version of OCaml that you are going to use to compile
> SMTCoq. In particular this means you want a version of Coq that was compiled
> with OCaml version >= 4.11.1.

### Install OCaml

Now you can install an OCaml compiler (we recommend 4.11.1):

```bash
opam switch create frocos23 ocaml-base-compiler.4.11.1
```

### Install Coq

After OCaml is installed, you can install Coq-8.20.0 through opam.

```bash
opam install coq.8.20.0
```

If you also want to install CoqIDE at the same time you can do

```bash
opam install coq.8.20.0 coqide.8.20.0
```
but you might need to install some extra packages and libraries for your system
(such as GTK2, gtksourceview2, etc.).


### Install CoqHammer

You can install CoqHammer through opam:

```bash
opam install coqhammer
```


## Install BVList and IC Proofs
Within root, run
```bash
coq_makefile -f _CoqProject -o Makefile
make
```
`BVList.v` is the bit-vector library; `InvCond.v` contains IC proofs over raw bit-vectors; `DepInvCond.v`
contains proofs of ICs over dependently-typed BVs.

1	We are trying to return to and solve our challenge problem.
2	The invertibility condition is for right shift and unsigned greater than on bit-vectors:
3	`(exists x, (x >> s) >u t) <=> (t <u (~s >> s))`,
4	and the challenging case is in the left-to-right direction of the equivalence:
5	`(exists x, (x >> s) >u t) => (t <u (~s >> s))`.
6	In my multiple approaches to prove this implication, it seems like I have diverged down multiple paths.
7	Broadly, there are the old and new attempts. Note that the labels `ltr` and `rtl` were inverted, so the 
8	same goal is called `bvshr_ugt_rtl` in the old attempt and `bvshr_ugt_ltr` in the new attempt. 
9	Either way, the Coq goal is:
10	```
11	forall (n : N), forall (s t : bitvector), 
12	  (size s) = n -> (size t) = n ->
13	    (exists (x : bitvector), (size x = n) /\ bv_ugt (bv_shr x s) t = true)
14	          ->
15	    (bv_ult t (bv_shr (bv_not s) s) = true).
16	```
17	
18	# Old Attempt
19	- Introduce premises, and skolemize existential premise.
20	- Simplify/unfold definitions. Importantly, replace `bv_shr` by alternative definition `bv_shr_a` which uses `skipn`.
21	- Use `rev_skipn` that proves
22	  ```
23	  rev_skipn: forall (b : bitvector) (n : nat), 
24	  (n < length b)%nat -> rev (skipn n b) = firstn (length b - n) (rev b).
25	  ```
26	  and simplify/unfold further.
27	- Case split on `toNat(s) < length(x)`
28	  1. If yes, 
29	    + Further simplify the context and goal, until we can use `rev_skipn` to replace
30	      the `skipn` in the goal with `firstn`.
31	    + Locally prove 
32	      ```
33	      [00..0] ++ firstn (length(x) - toNat(s)) (rev x)
34	                          <=u
35	      [00..0] ++ firstn (length(x) - toNat(s)) (rev (~s))
36	      ```
37	      which essentially reduces to `first_bits_ule` which proves the same thing as above with the `[00..0]` removed.
38	      ```
39	      firstn (length(x) - toNat(s)) (rev x)
40	                       <=u
41	      firstn (length(x) - toNat(s)) (rev (~s))
42	      ```
43	      which, in turn, reduces to `first_bits_zero`:
44	      ```
45	      toNat(s) < length(s) -> firstn (length(s) - toNat(s)) (rev s) = [00..0]
46	      ```
47	      and this is what we are trying to prove using 4 different approaches:
48	      1. induction on `length(s) - toNat(s)`; 
49	      2. induction on `length(s)` followed by 
50	      case splitting on `toNat(s)`, 
51	      3. induction on `length(s)` followed by 
52	      case splitting on `toNat(s)`, 
53	      4. induction on `toNat(s)` followed by 
54	      case splitting on `length(s)` 
55	      
56	      Approach 4 seems most promising (in terms
57	      of results) where for the induction on `toNat(s)`, I am able to prove both
58	      cases of the inductive case and the first case of the base case, and am
59	      only failing on the second case of the base case to prove 
60	      `length s = S n -> firstn (S n) (rev s) = mk_list_false (S n)` but this
61	      should be easy in theory, since in the base case `length(s) = 0`, but 
62	      Coq is not allowing me to retain this fact and use it in the proof.
63	  2. If no, then it is trivial to prove `t <u (~s >> s)`.
64	
65	
66	# New Attempt
67	There seems to be two approaches here.
68	## The `toNat` Approach
69	- Introduce premises, and skolemize existential premise.
70	- We don't rewrite `bv_shr` in terms of `bv_shr_a` simply because the 
71	  lemma here is already stated in terms of `bv_shr_a`.
72	- Change the `<u` in premise and conclusion to `<` over naturals.
73	- Then we do a lot of shit but essentially this reduces to 
74	  `skipn_bvnot`:
75	  ```
76	  forall (b : bitvector), toNat(b) < length (b) -> 
77	  skipn toNat(b) ~b = mk_list_true (length (b) - toNat(b)).
78	  ```
79	  which is essentially the same thing as `first_bits_zero` above
80	  with the direction and polarity of the BV reversed. But we 
81	  further reduce this to align the polarity in `skipn_b_zeros`:
82	  ```
83	  forall (b : bitvector), toNat(b) < length (b) -> 
84	  skipn toNat(b) b = mk_list_false (length (b) - toNat(b)).
85	  ```

and the challenging case is in the left-to-right direction of the equivalence:
`(exists x, (x >> s) >u t) => (t <u (~s >> s))`.
In my multiple approaches to prove this implication, it seems like I have diverged down multiple paths.
Broadly, there are the old and new attempts. Note that the labels `ltr` and `rtl` were inverted, so the 
same goal is called `bvshr_ugt_rtl` in the old attempt and `bvshr_ugt_ltr` in the new attempt. 
Either way, the Coq goal is:
```
forall (n : N), forall (s t : bitvector), 
  (size s) = n -> (size t) = n ->
    (exists (x : bitvector), (size x = n) /\ bv_ugt (bv_shr x s) t = true)
          ->

```

Require Import Lia.
Require Import Coq.Structures.Equalities.
Require Import ClassicalFacts.
Require Import Coq.Logic.Classical_Prop.
Require Import Coq.Reals.ArithProp.

Import ListNotations.
Local Open Scope list_scope.
Local Open Scope N_scope.
Local Open Scope bool_scope.




Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.

(* From Hammer Require Import Hammer Reconstr. *)
From BV Require Import Reconstr.

(* (* We temporarily assume proof irrelevance to handle dependently typed
   bit vectors *)
Axiom proof_irrelevance : forall (P : Prop) (p1 p2 : P), p1 = p2. *)

Lemma inj a a' : N.to_nat a = N.to_nat a' -> a = a'.
Proof. intros. lia. Qed.

  Fixpoint leb (n m: nat) : bool :=
    match n with
      | O => 
      match m with
        | O => true
        | S m' => true
      end
      | S n' =>
      match m with
        | O => false
        | S m' => leb n' m'
      end
    end.

(* From Hammer Require Import Hammer Reconstr. *)
From BV Require Import BVList Reconstr.

Import RAWBITVECTOR_LIST.

Require Import List Bool NArith Psatz (*Int63*) ZArith Nnat.



(*------------------------------Neg------------------------------*)


(* -x = t <=> True *)

Theorem bvneg_eq : forall (n : N), forall (t : bitvector),
  (size t) = n -> iff 
    True 
    (exists (x : bitvector), size x = n /\ bv_neg x = t).
Proof.
  intros n t Ht. split.
  + intros H. exists (bv_neg t). split.
    - apply bv_neg_size. apply Ht.
    - apply bv_neg_involutive. 
  + easy.
Qed.


(*------------------------------------------------------------*)


(*------------------------------Not------------------------------*)


(* ~x = t <=> True *)
Theorem bvnot_eq : forall (n : N), forall (t : bitvector),
 (size t) = n -> iff
    True
    (exists (x : bitvector), size x = n /\ bv_not x = t).
Proof.
  intros n t Ht. split; intros H.
  + exists (bv_not t). split.
    - apply bv_not_size. apply Ht.
    - apply bv_not_involutive.
  + easy.
Qed.

From BV Require Import BVList.

Import RAWBITVECTOR_LIST.

Open Scope nat_scope.

Theorem everything : 42 = 42.
Proof.
  reflexivity.
Qed.

Theorem plus_O_n : forall n : nat, 0 + n = n.
Proof.
  intros n.
  simpl.      (* Simplifies 0 + n to n *)
  reflexivity.
Qed.

Theorem plus_n_O : forall n : nat, n = n + 0.
Proof.
  intros n.
  induction n as [| n' IHn].
  - reflexivity.            (* Base case: 0 = 0 + 0 *)
  - simpl.                  (* Inductive step: S n' = S (n' + 0) *)
    rewrite <- IHn.         (* Use inductive hypothesis *)
    reflexivity.
Qed.

From Coq Require Import ZArith.
Open Scope Z_scope.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Overview

This is a Coq proof development for **bit-vector invertibility conditions** — formally proving equivalences of the form `(exists x, f(x) op t) <=> g(s, t)` over bitvectors. The main challenge is a right-shift/unsigned-greater-than invertibility condition.

All source lives in `bitvector/`.

## Build Commands

Run from within `bitvector/`:

```bash
# Regenerate Makefile (only needed if _CoqProject changes)
coq_makefile -f _CoqProject -o Makefile

# Compile all .v files
make

# Compile a single file
make BVList.vo
make InvCond.vo
make DepInvCond.vo
```

Requires: **Coq 8.20.0**, OCaml >= 4.11.1. Install via opam (see `bitvector/INSTALL.md`). CoqHammer is used in proofs but its tactics are bundled in `Reconstr.v`, so it is not required to compile.

## Architecture

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `BVList.v` | Core bitvector library. Defines raw (`RAWBITVECTOR_LIST`) and dependently-typed (`BITVECTOR_LIST`) bit-vector modules. All shared lemmas and helper tactics belong here. |
| `Reconstr.v` | Bundled CoqHammer reconstruction tactics (self-contained; no CoqHammer install needed). |
| `InvCond.v` | Proofs of 19 invertibility conditions over **raw** bitvectors. Imports `BVList` and `Reconstr`. |
| `DepInvCond.v` | Same IC proofs over **dependently-typed** bitvectors. |
| `coqPractice.v` | Scratch file for experimenting. |
| `BVListWorkbench.v` | Workbench for in-progress `BVList` lemmas. |

The `_CoqProject` file registers all `.v` files under the `BV` namespace (`-Q . BV`), so imports look like `From BV Require Import BVList`.

## Proof Style Conventions

(See `bitvector/conventions` for the authoritative list.)

- Pack multiple short tactics on one line up to a **60-character limit**; never split a single tactic across lines.
- Bullet points on their own lines; **no empty lines** between lines in a proof script (between `Proof.` and `Qed.`).
- Use whitespace only for bullet/subproof indentation, not arbitrary spacing.
- `InvCond.v` proofs should read like whiteboard proofs — push all complexity and generalized sublemmas into `BVList.v`. Only keep IC-specific subproofs in `InvCond.v`.

## Open Problem

The main unsolved goal is the left-to-right direction of the right-shift/unsigned-greater-than IC:

```coq
forall (n : N), forall (s t : bitvector),
  (size s) = n -> (size t) = n ->
    (exists (x : bitvector), (size x = n) /\ bv_ugt (bv_shr x s) t = true)
      ->
    (bv_ult t (bv_shr (bv_not s) s) = true).
```

See `bitvector/Notes.md` for a detailed history of proof attempts. The key subgoal is `skipn_b_zeros`:
```coq
forall (b : bitvector), toNat(b) < length(b) ->
  skipn toNat(b) b = mk_list_false (length(b) - toNat(b)).
```
